Subject: Re: Promo grant applied but tokens billed on invoice (VAT question)

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear screenshots. Short answer: the promo grant was issued and redeemed on your account, but there are two things that can make it look like "billed tokens" on the invoice: the usage ledger emits token usage lines first, and credits are applied as a separate ledger entry (credit application) which sometimes appears on a different invoice or as a credit memo.

Quick breakdown:
- Promo issuance: we granted the 30k tokens to your account on 2027-04-15 (you can see it in Account > Credits).
- Consumption: tokens used during the billing period create a usage charge line at the unit price; if credits exist they should reduce the invoice balance via an applied credit line.
- Timing mismatch: if the credit was applied after the invoice generation cut (or if credits are self-serve and pending reconciliation), the invoice will still show the usage line. The balance is resolved either by a subsequent credit memo or by the next invoice applying the leftover credit.

VAT note: Because Nebula is EU-registered, VAT treatment depends on whether you supplied a valid VAT ID in the account settings and whether the supply is considered B2B. If a VAT ID is on file we typically apply reverse-charge (0% VAT) and include the VAT ID on the invoice; if not, standard VAT may be added.

I'll do two things now:
1) Loop in Marissa from Sales to confirm the promo issuance metadata and whether we flagged this as a non-billable grant tied to the DA (deal DL-99842).
2) Ask Monica on Billing to check whether a credit memo was created or if we need to issue one so your finance team has a clear invoice + credit note for April.

I'll follow up once Monica confirms.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Claire — Monica from Billing here. Thanks for the attachments; that made this quick to triage.

What I found: the April invoice generated on 2027-04-21 before the PLG promo reconciliation job ran (the job runs overnight on the 22nd). Usage was therefore captured on the invoice as you saw; the promo credit was applied to the account on 2027-04-22 but after invoice generation.

Action I'm taking now:
- Issuing a credit memo (Credit Note CN-20270423-NEBLA) that offsets the 29,800 token charge. This credit memo will be linked to Invoice INV-20270421-NEBLA and will include the note: "Promo grant PROMO-20270415-NEBLA applied — non-billable promotional credit."
- VAT handling: because you have a valid EU VAT ID on file (checked: IE12345678), we'll mark the invoice reversal as reverse-charge; the credit memo will show 0% VAT and reference your VAT ID. If your accounting team requires a separate breakdown, I can add a line in the memo that explicitly states the VAT treatment.

Estimated timing: the credit memo PDF will be generated and emailed to you within 2 business hours; it will also appear in Account > Billing > Credits.

Claire, please confirm once you receive the credit memo and if your finance team needs any additional wording on the document.

Best,
Monica Patel
